explain.say: On the evening of 9 November 1989, thousands of East Berliners gathered at the checkpoints of the Berlin Wall. Near midnight the guards opened the gates, and people climbed onto the Wall and danced. For twenty-eight years it had split a city; at least 140 people died trying to cross it. Look at the timeline.

explain.say: Why did the system crack? See the causes. The Soviet economy was stagnating. Mikhail Gorbachev, leader from 1985, tried glasnost, openness, and perestroika, restructuring, but openness let criticism pour out. He also refused to send tanks to save Eastern European regimes. Which reform do you think backfired most?

draw.answer: A weak system, a reformer and brave crowds together.

explain.say: Now the map of 1989. In Poland, Solidarity won almost every seat it could contest in June. Hungary opened its border. Czechoslovakia's Velvet Revolution was peaceful; Romania's revolution was violent and its dictator was executed. One by one, communist regimes fell. Why did peaceful crowds succeed where tanks were once used?

Watch how the Wall actually opened. East Germans fled through Hungary, and huge crowds marched in Leipzig. On 9 November a party spokesman, Günter Schabowski, muddled a press conference and said new travel rules applied immediately. Crowds rushed to the checkpoints, and the guards gave way. Mary Elise Sarotte calls it an accidental opening. Which link was pure chance?

explain.say: Germany reunited in October 1990. After a failed hardline coup in August 1991, the Soviet republics broke away, Gorbachev resigned on 25 December, and the USSR ended. Did Reagan's pressure or inside decay matter more? Stephen Kotkin stresses decay. Superb work. Exam tip: weigh both, and give the people of 1989 their due.

draw.verdict: Most stress inside causes, plus outside pressure.

faq.q: Why did the Berlin Wall fall?
faq.a: Mass emigration through Hungary and huge protests, such as those in Leipzig, put East Germany's government under pressure. On 9 November 1989 spokesman Günter Schabowski mistakenly announced that new travel rules applied immediately, crowds gathered at the crossings and guards opened the gates.

Gorbachev's reforms from 1985. Glasnost, openness, relaxed censorship and allowed criticism. Perestroika, restructuring, tried to reform the planned economy. Together they weakened the Communist Party's control.

faq.q: Why did the Soviet Union collapse?
faq.a: A stagnant economy, falling oil prices, the costs of the arms race and the war in Afghanistan, Gorbachev's reforms, the loss of Eastern Europe in 1989, nationalist movements in the republics and a failed hardline coup in August 1991. It was dissolved in December 1991.

An independent trade union founded in Poland in 1980, led by the electrician Lech Wałęsa. Banned under martial law in 1981, it returned to win the partly free elections of June 1989, opening the way to the end of communism in Poland.

faq.q: Did Reagan win the Cold War?
faq.a: Some argue Reagan's arms build-up and pressure forced Soviet collapse. Many historians, such as Stephen Kotkin, stress internal economic decay, Gorbachev's choices and popular movements in 1989, while accepting that outside pressure played a part.

facts: The Berlin Wall was built in August 1961 and opened on 9 November 1989.
Gorbachev resigned on 25 December 1991 and the Soviet Union was dissolved the next day.

quiz.say: The Wall stood from August 1961 to November 1989. About how many years is that?

quiz.why: Glasnost was openness: less censorship and more public debate.
